summary: Steel lookout tower erected on Bellevue Hill in St. Albans by 1936; vandalized, then moved to Spruce Mountain in 1943 or 1944; the hilltop site is listed as gone.

facts.design: Steel tower with a 7x7 foot steel cab
facts.status_note: The hilltop site is listed as gone. The steel tower itself was moved to Spruce Mountain in Plainfield, where it still stands.

events.note: State accepted the hill as a park and picnic ground and authorized $1,500 to landscape the summit and erect a lookout tower; the St. Albans Chamber of Commerce had been raising $500 for a clear title to 35 acres
Steel lookout tower erected on Bellevue Hill, per an April 1936 Burlington Free Press report; the report gives no exact construction date
July 1938 report: vandals smashed windows and defaced walls; the state forester said the house and tower had both been damaged and announced the tower would be removed
Steel tower with 7x7 steel cab moved to Spruce Mountain; the Register and the Forest Lookouts page give 1943, the state forest page gives 1944

corrections.why: The hilltop site is gone, but the steel tower was moved to Spruce Mountain in 1943 or 1944 and still stands there, so the record should show the tower moved.

resolved_conflicts.field: year of move to Spruce Mountain
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register and the Forest Lookouts page date the move to 1943; the state forest page dates it to 1944. The story gives both dates and does not choose between them.

notes_for_editor: The 1936 build date is the date of the newspaper report, not a stated construction year. The 1943/1944 move year conflicts across sources (see resolved_conflicts). A search for what the Bellevue Hill site looks like now found only Aldis Hill in St. Albans, a different place, so nothing was used. Access to the hilltop is not described by any source found. The Spruce Mountain story (us-vt-spruce-mountain) already covers the move and can be cross-linked.
